You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC notes: opposite-edge bar projection

Observed task family from task-7c9e82e3. Useful for future recurring instances.

## Rule inferred from demonstrations and the solved instance
- Grid has a uniform background, two matching short solid bars on opposite borders, and one or more isolated marker pixels of another color.
- Bars are aligned perpendicular to the marker rays (e.g. horizontal bars at top/bottom imply vertical lines; vertical bars at left/right imply horizontal lines).
- Each marker is associated with the border bar segment that contains its perpendicular coordinate (its position along the bar). Extend a line in the marker's original color from the marker toward that border along its own row/column, stopping at the border.
- Match the marker's offset within that bar segment to the same offset in the opposite-edge bar. Draw a full line of the marker color at that opposite-edge coordinate between the borders. Preserve both bars.
- Change the original marker pixel to color 4.
- Where lines meet a marker, marker becomes 4; other line pixels use the marker's original color. Do not change unrelated cells.

## Verified test interpretation
Top bar color 2 at row 0, columns 3–5; bottom bar at row 13, columns 0–2. Marker pixels color 3 at (r3,c4), (r7,c3), (r7,c5). Each is positioned over the top bar's 3-cell span, offsets 1,0,2 respectively:
- Draw vertical line at opposite-bar columns c1,c0,c2 (all rows between bars); top row cells c0–2 become 3, while bottom bar stays 2.
- Draw own-column extensions toward top at c4 through r2, and c3/c5 through r6; turn the marker cells at (3,4),(7,3),(7,5) to 4.
This exact output was accepted.

Demo 7 had top bar c0–3 and bottom bar c4–7, background 3; marker color 8 at (r4,c7), within bottom bar's span at offset 3. Output drew the full corresponding opposite-bar line at c3 (rows 1–9), continued the marker's own c7 line toward the bottom border (r5–8), and changed the marker to 4. Bars remained unchanged.

## Other observed examples
- Horizontal/vertical cases both occur: rotate the same rule when bars are on left/right edges.
- Marker colors may vary (e.g. 0, 1, 8, 9); line uses that marker color and marker itself becomes 4.
- Multiple markers can project to several counterpart lines; if markers share a counterpart coordinate, merge lines.

Earlier incorrect attempts filled entire regions or entire bar widths instead of just the marker's own ray plus the offset-matched full counterpart line.
